title: A router in front of many experts
brief: Build router/ so one program can hold several experts and send each task to the right one. You write a small RPC client for one expert process, put the shared rules in a base pack, create one SDK session per expert with its own prompt, tools and session folder, and write the router: cheap rules first, then a classifier session that can only answer sql, k8s, quant or unsure. Every decision goes to a log. You add a chain that hands one expert's answer to the next and stops at three steps. When you finish, a task such as "Monthly revenue in Germany for 2025" reaches the SQL expert, an unclear task asks the user, and a two-part task runs as a logged chain. Code tests use stub experts. Real runs need DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.

starter.note: New. Spawns pi --mode rpc, writes a prompt command, waits for agent_settled, then asks get_last_assistant_text. Answers extension_ui_request so a dialog never waits forever.
Edit. Add the house_rules section, a gate that blocks any argument containing DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, a fleet-log entry on tool_result, and keep the scrubbed bash.
New. makeExpert(name, promptFile, extensionFactory, tools) returns a session. sql uses agents/sql/sessions.
New. route(task): rules, then the classifier, then experts[choice].prompt(task). Unsure returns a question for the user.
New. A session with no tools except choose_expert, whose parameter is a string enum of sql, k8s, quant, unsure, with terminate true.
New. Runs up to 3 steps, fills {previous} with the last answer and logs each step.
New. Tests with stub experts and a fake child process for RPC. No network.

hints: Closing stdin shuts the RPC process down. The prompt response only says it started; the answer is ready at the agent_settled event.
Frame RPC as one JSON object per line and split on newline only. It is not JSON-RPC 2.0: messages have type and an optional id.
Load the base pack first. Handlers run in load order, and the first tool_call handler that blocks ends the chain, so base gates run before the domain ones.
In SDK sessions, MCP and codemode are not loaded unless you add them. Raise PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS if several experts use codemode in one process.
Put the router rules in a plain function that takes the task and returns an expert name or undefined, so you can test it with no session at all.
Log every decision as one JSON line in router/decisions.jsonl: task, choice, reason. Wrong routes become golden tasks later.
Hand off through the router, not through an expert calling another. Each expert then keeps its own guards and only sees its own part.

rubric.criterion: A print or JSON run is used for one-off tasks, and rpc-expert.ts documents which mode it uses and why, with an exit code check where print mode is used
rpc-expert.ts sends one JSON command per line, waits for agent_settled rather than the prompt response, and answers extension dialogs
makeExpert builds one SDK session per expert with its own prompt, tools, extension factories and session folder, and session.prompt resolves after the run
The base pack loads first, adds the house_rules section, blocks arguments that contain the key name, and appends a fleet-log entry without sending it to the model
route applies rules first, then a classifier that can only answer from the allowed set, logs every decision, and asks the user when the answer is unsure
chain.ts passes one answer into the next task through {previous}, caps the chain at 3 steps and logs each step

milestones.title: Drive one expert over RPC
milestones.body: Write rpc-expert.ts. The test starts a small fake process that speaks the same line protocol: a prompt response with disposition started, events, agent_settled, then get_last_assistant_text. The client must return the text only after agent_settled. A run against the real SQL expert needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.

milestones.title: The base pack
milestones.body: Extend packs/base/extension.ts. With the fake pi, check that house_rules is added in before_agent_start, that an argument holding DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is blocked, and that a tool_result appends a fleet-log entry with the tool name and duration.

milestones.title: One SDK session per expert
milestones.body: Write experts.ts. The test builds the sql expert with the base pack first, checks that its session folder is agents/sql/sessions, and that two experts do not share a session folder. A real prompt through one session needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.

milestones.title: Rules, classifier and the decision log
milestones.body: Write the rules, the classifier and route. A task that mentions pod goes to k8s by rule. A stubbed classifier answering unsure must return a question for the user. Every call must add one line to router/decisions.jsonl.

milestones.title: Hand off between experts
milestones.body: Write chain.ts. With a stub sql expert that returns twelve numbers and a stub quant expert, the second task must contain the first answer in place of {previous}. A chain of four steps must stop at three and say so.
